title: Context and memory in the makerspace assistant

items.stem: On Monday a student tells your assistant, "I finished CNC router training." On Thursday the same student opens a new chat. Your program saved nothing between the two chats and sends only the instructions and the new question. What does the model know about the student's CNC training?

options.text: It still knows, because the model keeps every past chat
It knows only if the student asks about the CNC router
It knows nothing, because the new window never contained it
It knows, because Monday's window was larger than Thursday's

items.stem: In one request, the first model call reads 1,000 input tokens. Each later call re-sends everything before it plus 500 new tokens (the previous request and its tool result). The model is called 4 times in total. How many input tokens does the model read across all 4 calls?

Your team learns that a new model has a context window big enough to hold all the makerspace manuals at once. A teammate says retrieval is now unnecessary. Which reply is best for a small model budget?

options.text: Agreed, since a window that fits the manuals removes any cost
Agreed, since a model reads long text as well as short
Disagree, because the model would then forget the students
Disagree, because every call would re-read the manuals and pay for them

items.stem: A request that takes ten tool calls costs far more than ten times the cost of a request with one model call and no tools. In one sentence, why?

A student asks about the maximum thickness for the laser cutter, and the assistant quotes the figure for the 3D printer. You find the search returned three chunks, all from the 3D printer manual. What is the best first step?

options.text: Switch to a bigger model so that it reads more carefully
Add the laser manual to the saved notes for every student
Log the returned chunks and test the search on this question
Tell the model in its instructions to never quote a figure
